reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of CD52 target engagement - severe lymphopenia and CD4 depletion indicate alemtuzumab successfully bound CD52 and depleted lymphocytes as intended. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The mechanism appears to have worked - combination of CD52-mediated lymphocyte depletion plus cytotoxic chemotherapy produced the intended biological effect of eliminating leukemic cells. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: 33% complete response rate suggests meaningful clinical activity, though without a control arm or statistical testing, significance is unclear. For relapsed/refractory ALL, this response rate could be clinically meaningful. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported in this small study. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Major limitation is the very small sample size (n=12) making it impossible to draw definitive conclusions about efficacy. Single-arm design prevents comparison to standard of care.

failure_modes.evidence: Sample size of only 12 patients is extremely small for evaluating efficacy in relapsed/refractory ALL, preventing definitive conclusions about treatment effect
